newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian preacher to be tried after Java riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian preacher to be tried after Java riot.

text.p: An Indonesian Moslem preacher would be tried soon on charges of inciting riots in central Java prior to the May 29 general elections, a prosecutor said on Wednesday.
"Afifudin Musytari will be tried soon for allegedly inciting riots in Pekalongan through his speeches," the prosecutor told Reuters from Pekalongan, 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta.
He said the trial would likely be held in Semarang, capital of Java province.

"He has been accused of violating the article number 160 of the criminal code," the prosecutor said, referring to the offence of inciting riots, which carries a maximum penalty of six years in jail. He declined to give further details.

Riots broke out in Pekalongan in March after local government officials removed the flags of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) from the streets and replaced them with the flags from the ruling Golkar party.
Rioters vandalised a number of shops and properties of local ethnic Chinese in Pekalongan, which is a PPP stronghold.
In one isolated case, angry PPP loyalists set fire to a stage that was to be used in a Golkar rally that featured a singer who previously was a supporter of the Moslem-based party.
The Jakarta Post reported on Wednesday that Musytari, 46, had said he did not mean to insult Golkar or any ethnic group when he addressed a gathering before the riots.
Widespread rioting, mostly on Java, marred the 27-day campaign for the general elections, which Golkar swept with more than 74 percent of the vote.
Authorities have said more than 300 people died during the campaign, mostly in traffic accidents, while 124 died in a shopping centre fire during a riot in South Kalimantan.
The PPP won just under 23 percent of the vote and the badly split Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) won only three percent.
